agent_authored.description: Complete SfePy finite-element capability map: 19 module proposals across solid mechanics, scalar transport, fluid flow, waves, quantum eigenproblems and coupled/multiscale physics. The existing static-elasticity direction was accepted in source PR #608; all new modules require review.

source_review.scope: Original static-linear-elasticity cut at a57fbffb596376e3715d645d3f8771bb2801bb77 only. Expanded examples and file ownership in this plan remain proposed revisions.

agent_authored.domain_note: Retagged to materials-engineering with primary physics.app-ph, secondary physics.comp-ph, following source-review item 7. Individual future task science tags need module-specific selection, e.g. quant-ph for the quantum module.

measurement.regular_file_rule: all regular files below the source snapshot
measurement.physical_line_rule: UTF-8/NUL-free bytes: newline count plus one final non-newline line
measurement.text_binary_rule: NUL-containing or non-UTF-8 files are binary for line accounting
measurement.directory_rule: count non-root directory ancestors containing an included regular file or symlink
measurement.symlink_rule: count links without following them; external/parent targets are redacted

agent_authored.generated_vendor_third_party_notes: Complete unmodified git archive of release_2026.2. No extra payload, repository metadata or local build artifacts. Python pathlib physical-line counter includes comments and blank lines: Python 408 files/113701 lines; Cython 16/5436; C 28/15823; C headers 31/1740. AST walk counted test_ function/method definitions. Example Python file counts include helpers, not only independent cases.
agent_authored.inventory_semantics: Every one of the 137 Python files under sfepy/examples is assigned to a physics module, shared support, an initializer, or a non-scientific logging demo. Scenario/driver files are not finalized suitable checks; configuration chains and interface variants are not counted as independent checks merely because they are separate files.

shared_components.title: Shared finite-element runtime, physical kernels and cross-cutting tests
shared_components.purpose: Mesh/basis/DOF/constraint machinery, sparse and time/eigen solvers, linear/diffusion/hyperelastic/DG kernels and bindings, common material tensors, homogenization orchestration, application I/O and tests used across the module map.
shared_components.relationship: A common source pool reused by the module configurations; membership does not claim every module executes every shared path. Specialized execution paths are named on each module card.
